stem: Ravi scores $15$ marks out of $20$ on one test and $20$ marks out of $25$ on another.

parts.text: Which claim about comparing his percentages is correct?

options.text: Write $15/20 = 75\%$ and $20/25 = 80\%$; the wholes differ, so compare those percentages rather than the raw marks alone.
$20 > 15$, so the second score is the higher percentage without converting.
Compare the raw marks $20$ and $15$ directly while the totals stay $25$ and $20$.
A fair percentage comparison forces the totals $20$ and $25$ to be equal before any calculation.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Different wholes mean raw marks are not comparable; convert each to a percentage (or common whole) first: $75\%$ versus $80\%$.

teacher.key_rationale: 15/20=75% and 20/25=80%. Compare percentages, not raw marks. B/C omit base conversion. D wrongly requires equal totals first.
